docs.preview:
**Please include the full output of youtube-dl when run with `-v`**, i.e. **add** `-v` flag to **your command line**, copy the **whole** output and post it in the issue body wrapped in \`\`\` for better formatting. It should look similar to this:
```
$ youtube-dl -v <your command line>
[debug] System config: []
[debug] User config: []
[debug] Command-line args: [u'-v', u'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BaW_jenozKcj']
[debug] Encodings: locale cp1251, fs mbcs, out cp866, pref cp1251
[debug] youtube-dl version 2015.12.06
[debug] Git HEAD: 135392e
[debug] Python version 2.6.6 - Windows-2003Server-5.2.3790-SP2
[debug] exe versions: ffmpeg N-75573-g1d0487f, ffprobe N-75573-g1d0487f, rtmpdump 2.4
[debug] Proxy map: {}
...
```
**Do not post screenshots of verbose logs; only plain text is acceptable.**

The output (including the first lines) contains important debugging information. Issues without the full output are often not reproducible and therefore do not get solved in short order, if ever.

Please re-read your issue once again to avoid a couple of common mistakes (you can and should use this as a checklist):

### Is the description of the issue itself sufficient?

We often get issue reports that we cannot really decipher. While in most cases we eventually get the required information after asking back multiple times, this poses an unnecessary drain on our resources. Many contributors, including myself, are also not native speakers, so we may misread some parts.

So please elaborate on what feature you are requesting, or what bug you want to be fixed. Make sure that it's obvious

- What the problem is
- How it could be fixed
- How your proposed solution would look like

If your report is shorter than two lines, it is almost certainly missing some of these, which makes it hard for us to respond to it. We're often too polite to close the issue outright, but the missing info makes misinterpretation likely. As a committer myself, I often get frustrated by these issues, since the only possible way for me to move forward on them is to ask for clarification over and over.

For bug reports, this means that your report should contain the *complete* output of youtube-dl when called with the `-v` flag. The error message you get for (most) bugs even says so, but you would not believe how many of our bug reports do not contain this information.

If your server has multiple IPs or you suspect censorship, adding `--call-home` may be a good idea to get more diagnostics. If the error is `ERROR: Unable to extract ...` and you cannot reproduce it from multiple countries, add `--dump-pages` (warning: this will yield a rather large output, redirect it to the file `log.txt` by adding `>log.txt 2>&1` to your command-line) or upload the `.dump` files you get when you add `--write-pages` [somewhere](https://gist.github.com/).

**Site support requests must contain an example URL**. An example URL is a URL you might want to download, like `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BaW_jenozKc`. There should be an obvious video present. Except under very special circumstances, the main page of a video service (e.g. `https://www.youtube.com/`) is *not* an example URL.

###  Are you using the latest version?

Before reporting any issue, type `youtube-dl -U`. This should report that you're up-to-date. About 20% of the reports we receive are already fixed, but people are using outdated versions. This goes for feature requests as well.

###  Is the issue already documented?

Make sure that someone has not already opened the issue you're trying to open. Search at the top of the window or browse the [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/search?type=Issues) of this repository. If there is an issue, feel free to write something along the lines of "This affects me as well, with version 2015.01.01. Here is some more information on the issue: ...". While some issues may be old, a new post into them often spurs rapid activity.

###  Why are existing options not enough?

Before requesting a new feature, please have a quick peek at [the list of supported options](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/blob/master/README.md#options). Many feature requests are for features that actually exist already! Please, absolutely do show off your work in the issue report and detail how the existing similar options do *not* solve your problem.

###  Is there enough context in your bug report?

People want to solve problems, and often think they do us a favor by breaking down their larger problems (e.g. wanting to skip already downloaded files) to a specific request (e.g. requesting us to look whether the file exists before downloading the info page). However, what often happens is that they break down the problem into two steps: One simple, and one impossible (or extremely complicated one).

We are then presented with a very complicated request when the original problem could be solved far easier, e.g. by recording the downloaded video IDs in a separate file. To avoid this, you must include the greater context where it is non-obvious. In particular, every feature request that does not consist of adding support for a new site should contain a use case scenario that explains in what situation the missing feature would be useful.

###  Does the issue involve one problem, and one problem only?

Some of our users seem to think there is a limit of issues they can or should open. There is no limit of issues they can or should open. While it may seem appealing to be able to dump all your issues into one ticket, that means that someone who solves one of your issues cannot mark the issue as closed. Typically, reporting a bunch of issues leads to the ticket lingering since nobody wants to attack that behemoth, until someone mercifully splits the issue into multiple ones.

In particular, every site support request issue should only pertain to services at one site (generally under a common domain, but always using the same backend technology). Do not request support for vimeo user videos, White house podcasts, and Google Plus pages in the same issue. Also, make sure that you don't post bug reports alongside feature requests. As a rule of thumb, a feature request does not include outputs of youtube-dl that are not immediately related to the feature at hand. Do not post reports of a network error alongside the request for a new video service.

###  Is anyone going to need the feature?

Only post features that you (or an incapacitated friend you can personally talk to) require. Do not post features because they seem like a good idea. If they are really useful, they will be requested by someone who requires them.

###  Is your question about youtube-dl?

It may sound strange, but some bug reports we receive are completely unrelated to youtube-dl and relate to a different, or even the reporter's own, application. Please make sure that you are actually using youtube-dl. If you are using a UI for youtube-dl, report the bug to the maintainer of the actual application providing the UI. On the other hand, if your UI for youtube-dl fails in some way you believe is related to youtube-dl, by all means, go ahead and report the bug.

# DEVELOPER INSTRUCTIONS

Most users do not need to build youtube-dl and can [download the builds](https://ytdl-org.github.io/youtube-dl/download.html) or get them from their distribution.

To run youtube-dl as a developer, you don't need to build anything either. Simply execute

    python -m youtube_dl

To run the test, simply invoke your favorite test runner, or execute a test file directly; any of the following work:

    python -m unittest discover
    python test/test_download.py
    nosetests

See item 6 of [new extractor tutorial](#adding-support-for-a-new-site) for how to run extractor specific test cases.

If you want to create a build of youtube-dl yourself, you'll need

* python
* make (only GNU make is supported)
* pandoc
* zip
* nosetests

### Adding support for a new site

If you want to add support for a new site, first of all **make sure** this site is **not dedicated to [copyright infringement](README.md#can-you-add-support-for-this-anime-video-site-or-site-which-show

# INSTALLATION

To install it right away for all UNIX users (Linux, macOS, etc.), type:

    sudo curl -L https://yt-dl.org/downloads/latest/youtube-dl -o /usr/local/bin/youtube-dl
    sudo chmod a+rx /usr/local/bin/youtube-dl

If you do not have curl, you can alternatively use a recent wget:

    sudo wget https://yt-dl.org/downloads/latest/youtube-dl -O /usr/local/bin/youtube-dl
    sudo chmod a+rx /usr/local/bin/youtube-dl

Windows users can [download an .exe file](https://yt-dl.org/latest/youtube-dl.exe) and place it in any location on their [PATH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PATH_%28variable%29) except for `%SYSTEMROOT%\System32` (e.g. **do not** put in `C:\Windows\System32`).

You can also use pip:

    sudo -H pip install --upgrade youtube-dl

This command will update youtube-dl if you have already installed it. See the [pypi page](https://pypi.python.org/pypi/youtube_dl) for more information.

macOS users can install youtube-dl with [Homebrew](https://brew.sh/):

    brew install youtube-dl

Or with [MacPorts](https://www.macports.org/):

    sudo port install youtube-dl

Alternatively, refer to the [developer instructions](#developer-instructions) for how to check out and work with the git repository. For further options, including PGP signatures, see the [youtube-dl Download Page](https://ytdl-org.github.io/youtube-dl/download.html).

# DESCRIPTION
**youtube-dl** is a command-line program to download videos from YouTube.com and a few more sites. It requires the Python interpreter, version 2.6, 2.7, or 3.2+, and it is not platform specific. It should work on your Unix box, on Windows or on macOS. It is released to the public domain, which means you can modify it, redistribute it or use it however you like.

    youtube-dl [OPTIONS] URL [URL...]

# OPTIONS
    -h, --help                           Print this help text and exit
    --version                            Print program version and exit
    -U, --update                         Update this program to latest version.
                                         Make sure that you have sufficient
                                         permissions (run with sudo if needed)
    -i, --ignore-errors                  Continue on download errors, for
                                         example to skip unavailable videos in a
                                         playlist
    --abort-on-error                     Abort downloading of further videos (in
                                         the playlist or the command line) if an
                                         error occurs
    --dump-user-agent                    Display the current browser
                                         identification
    --list-extractors                    List all supported extractors
    --extractor-descriptions             Output descriptions of all supported
                                         extractors
    --force-generic-extractor            Force extraction to use the generic
                                         extractor
    --default-search PREFIX              Use this prefix for unqualified URLs.
                                         For example "gvsearch2:" downloads two
                                         videos from google videos for youtube-
                                         dl "large apple". Use the value "auto"
                                         to let youtube-dl guess ("auto_warning"
                                         to emit a warning when guessing).
                                         "error" just throws an error. The
                                         default value "fixup_error" repairs
                                         broken URLs, but emits an error if this
                                         is not possible instead of searching.
    --ignore-config                      Do not read configuration files. When
                                         given in the global configuration file
                                         /etc/youtube-dl.conf: Do not read the
                                         user configuration in
                                         ~/.config/youtube-dl/config
                                         (%APPDATA%/youtube-dl/config.txt on
                                         Windows)
    --config-location PATH               Location of the configuration file;
                                         either the path to the config or its
                                         containing directory.
    --flat-playlist                      Do not extract the videos of a
                                         playlist, only list them.
    --mark-watched                       Mark videos watched (YouTube only)
    --no-mark-watched                    Do not mark videos watched (YouTube
                                         only)
    --no-color                           Do not emit color codes in output

## Network Options:
    --proxy URL                          Use the specified HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS
                                         proxy. To enable SOCKS proxy, specify a
                                         proper scheme. For example
                                         socks5://127.0.0.1:1080/. Pass in an
                                         empty string (--proxy "") for direct
                                         connection
    --socket-timeout SECONDS             Time to wait before giving up, in
                                         seconds
    --source-address IP                  Client-side IP address to bind to
    -4, --force-ipv4                     Make all connections via IPv4
    -6, --force-ipv6                     Make all connections via IPv6

## Geo Restriction:
    --geo-verification-proxy URL         Use this proxy to verify the IP address
                                         for some geo-restricted sites. The
                                         default proxy specified by --proxy (or
                                         none, if the option is not present) is
                                         used for the actual downloading.
    --geo-bypass                         Bypass geographic restriction via
                                         faking X-Forwarded-For HTTP header
    --no-geo-bypass                      Do not bypass geographic restriction
                                         via faking X-Forwarded-For HTTP header
    --geo-bypass-country CODE            Force bypass geographic restriction
                                         with explicitly provided two-letter ISO
                                         3166-2 country code
    --geo-bypass-ip-block IP_BLOCK       Force bypass geographic restriction
                                         with explicitly provided IP block in
                                         CIDR notation

## Video Selection:
    --playlist-start NUMBER              Playlist video to start at (default is
                                         1)
    --playlist-end NUMBER                Playlist video to end at (default is
                                         last)
    --playlist-items ITEM_SPEC           Playlist video items to download.
                                         Specify indices of the videos in the
                                         playlist separated by commas like: "--
                                         playlist-items 1,2,5,8" if you want to

report.overview: youtube-dl is a dependency-free Python command-line program (and embeddable library) that downloads video and audio from YouTube and ~1200 other sites. A single YoutubeDL orchestrator class routes each user-supplied URL to the first matching InfoExtractor (regex-matched from a registry of ~810 extractor modules), normalizes the returned 'info dict', selects a format via a small DSL, downloads via a protocol-mapped FileDownloader (native HTTP/HLS/DASH or external tools like ffmpeg/aria2c), and runs a postprocessor chain (ffmpeg muxing, metadata, thumbnails). It still maintains Python 2.6 compatibility through a large compat shim and ships as a pip package, a self-updating single-file zip executable, and a py2exe Windows binary.

system_map.summary: The system is a monolithic Python package `youtube_dl` with a layered pipeline: CLI parsing (options.py) -> orchestrator (YoutubeDL.py) -> site extractors (extractor/*) -> protocol downloaders (downloader/*) -> postprocessors (postprocessor/*). Shared helpers live in an enormous utils.py and a Python 2/3 compat.py shim. Distribution is via setuptools console script, a Makefile-built single-file zipapp `youtube-dl`, and py2exe; self-update is built in via update.py against yt-dl.org. There is no persistent daemon or service: state is limited to a JSON filesystem cache, a Netscape-format cookie jar, and a download-archive text file.

claims.claim: The CLI has three equivalent entrypoints: `python -m youtube_dl` (youtube_dl/__main__.py calls youtube_dl.main()), the `bin/youtube-dl` wrapper script, and the setuptools console_scripts entry `youtube-dl = youtube_dl:main` in setup.py.

All CLI startup logic is `_real_main` in youtube_dl/__init__.py: it calls parseOpts, mutates the global `std_headers` dict for --user-agent/--referer/--add-header, validates option combinations, builds the ~120-key `ydl_opts` dict, then runs `ydl.download(all_urls)` inside a `with YoutubeDL(ydl_opts)` context.

`YoutubeDL` (YoutubeDL.py) is the central orchestrator: it holds `params`, a list `_ies` of InfoExtractors, `_pps` postprocessors, `cookiejar`, `cache`, and `_opener` (a urllib OpenerDirector); its class docstring enumerates the full options contract used by CLI and library consumers.

The extractor subsystem is a flat package of ~810 modules under youtube_dl/extractor/, each defining InfoExtractor subclasses; they are aggregated by youtube_dl/extractor/extractors.py into `_ALL_CLASSES` (GenericIE appended last) or, for release builds, by a generated `lazy_extractors.py` module.

The downloader layer maps an info dict's `protocol` field to a FileDownloader subclass via PROTOCOL_MAP (rtmp, m3u8_native->HlsFD, m3u8->FFmpegFD, mms/rtsp->RtspFD, f4m, http_dash_segments, ism, niconico_dmc), defaulting to HttpFD.

The postprocessor layer is a small registry: `get_postprocessor(key)` resolves `key + 'PP'` in the module globals; built-ins include FFmpegExtractAudioPP, FFmpegVideoConvertorPP, FFmpegMetadataPP, FFmpegEmbedSubtitlePP, FFmpegMergerPP, EmbedThumbnailPP, XAttrMetadataPP, MetadataFromTitlePP and ExecAfterDownloadPP.

youtube_dl/utils.py (6863 lines) is the shared toolbox: it defines `std_headers`, `sanitized_Request`, the custom urllib handlers (YoutubeDLHandler, YoutubeDLRedirectHandler, YoutubeDLCookieProcessor, PerRequestProxyHandler), `YoutubeDLCookieJar`, `sanitize_filename`, `GeoUtils`, `match_filter_func`, exception classes, and `DEFAULT_OUTTMPL`.

youtube_dl/compat.py (3901 lines) is a hand-rolled Python 2.6-3.x compatibility layer aliasing stdlib names as `compat_*` symbols; setup.py classifiers advertise Python 2.6 through 3.8 plus Jython/PyPy/IronPython.

All HTTP(S) traffic goes through `YoutubeDL._setup_opener`, which builds a urllib opener from PerRequestProxyHandler, a params-aware HTTPS handler, YoutubeDLCookieProcessor, YoutubeDLHandler (compression + URL fixups), YoutubeDLRedirectHandler, a DataHandler, and a FileHandler whose `file_open` is stubbed to disable the file:// scheme for security.

The release build produces a self-contained executable: Makefile target `youtube-dl` copies the package into a zip with a `__main__.py` at the zip root, prepends a python shebang and chmod +x; Windows builds use py2exe options embedded in setup.py.

Filesystem cache is implemented by `Cache` in youtube_dl/cache.py storing JSON under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/youtube-dl` (or --cache-dir), keyed by section/key, versioned per release with a minimum-version invalidation check.

External executables are runtime dependencies probed lazily: ffmpeg/avconv/ffprobe located by FFmpegPostProcessor._determine_executables, rtmpdump via downloader/rtmp.py's rtmpdump_version, and phantomjs via extractor/openload.py's PhantomJSwrapper._version; all three are reported in the verbose debug header.

Tests and lint are driven by `nosetests` (test/ directory, ~34 test modules) via Makefile `test`/`offlinetest` targets and devscripts/run_tests.sh, plus a `flake8 .` codetest target configured in setup.cfg.

feature_catalog.summary: User-facing surface = one CLI command `youtube-dl` with ~200 options defined in options.py plus the embeddable YoutubeDL API. Features cluster around: site extraction (~1200 supported sites), format/playlist/subtitle selection, sidecar file output (info JSON, description, annotations, thumbnails), ffmpeg-based postprocessing (audio extraction, recoding, embedding), authentication (username/password, netrc, video passwords, Adobe Pass TV providers), geo-restriction bypass, external downloaders, self-update, and simulation/printing modes for scripting.

claims.claim: Site support: ~810 extractor modules under youtube_dl/extractor/ back roughly 1225 documented sites in docs/supportedsites.md; `--list-extractors` and `--extractor-descriptions` enumerate them at runtime via list_extractors().

Format selection via `-f/--format` implements a mini-DSL (best/worst, format_id, filters like `[height<=?720]`, merge with `+`, fallback with `/`, groups) parsed by `YoutubeDL.build_format_selector` into selector functions.

Playlist features include --playlist-start/--playlist-end, --playlist-items (comma list/ranges), --playlist-reverse, --playlist-random, --max-downloads, and --flat-playlist (extract_flat), implemented in __process_playlist.

Subtitle support: --write-sub/--write-auto-subs/--all-subs/--list-subs download or enumerate subtitle tracks, with --sub-format and --sub-langs filtering in process_subtitles; --convert-subs converts to srt/ass/vtt/lrc via FFmpegSubtitlesConvertorPP.

Audio extraction `-x/--extract-audio` appends an FFmpegExtractAudio postprocessor honoring --audio-format (best/aac/flac/mp3/m4a/opus/vorbis/wav) and --audio-quality; recoding via --recode-video maps to FFmpegVideoConvertorPP.

Sidecar outputs: --write-info-json, --write-description, --write-annotations, --write-thumbnail/--write-all-thumbnails, and --xattrs (filesystem extended attributes) are all emitted from process_info/_write_info_json/_write_thumbnails.

--download-archive records `extractor_key + ' ' + video_id` lines (via _make_archive_id) into a text file; in_download_archive checks it inside _match_entry to skip already-downloaded videos; writes go through locked_file for interprocess safety.

Authentication options cover --username/--password (+ interactive getpass when password omitted), --twofactor, --netrc, --video-password, and Adobe Pass TV-provider login via --ap-mso/--ap-username/--ap-password with --ap-list-mso listing MSO_INFO providers.

Self-update: `-U/--update` invokes update_self(), which only applies to the zip/frozen builds, verifies a pinned RSA signature over versions.json, then sha256-checks and replaces the running binary (via a .bat swap on Windows).

Geo-bypass fakes an X-Forwarded-For header with a random IP drawn from per-extractor _GEO_COUNTRIES/_GEO_IP_BLOCKS or --geo-bypass-country/--geo-bypass-ip-block, with automatic retry on GeoRestrictedError inside InfoExtractor.extract.

External downloaders: --external-downloader selects among aria2c, aria2p (JSON-RPC library), axel, curl, ffmpeg/avconv, httpie and wget; each ExternalFD subclass builds a CLI via _make_cmd and runs it with subprocess.Popen; --external-downloader-args injects extra args.

Simulation/inspection modes: --simulate, --skip-download, --dump-json/--dump-single-json, --print-json, --get-url/--get-title/--get-id/--get-filename family, --list-formats and --list-thumbnails, plus --load-info-json to reprocess a saved info dict.

Output templating `-o` supports %(field)s substitution over the info dict (plus `epoch`, `autonumber`), NA placeholders, numeric-field format patching, env-var/`~` expansion, and `outtmpl='-'` to stream media to stdout.
--exec CMD registers ExecAfterDownloadPP which substitutes `{}` with the shlex-quoted final filepath and runs the command through the system shell after all other postprocessing.

Rate/robustness controls: --limit-rate (throttling via FileDownloader.slow_down), --retries/--fragment-retries (incl. 'inf'), --sleep-interval/--max-sleep-interval randomized delays, --http-chunk-size segmented downloading, --buffer-size and --no-resize-buffer adaptive block sizing.

data_flow.summary: Data moves in one direction through a well-defined pipeline. Inputs: CLI args + config files + batch files produce a URL list; the params dict is the single source of truth shared by all layers. Extractors turn a URL into an 'info dict' (a documented schema with _type discriminators video/url/url_transparent/playlist); process_ie_result resolves indirection recursively; process_video_result normalizes fields and selects formats; process_info emits sidecar files and invokes a protocol-matched FileDownloader that writes .part files and renames on completion; the postprocessor chain mutates/moves the final file; bookkeeping lands in the download archive, cookie jar, and JSON cache.

claims.claim: URL input boundary: positional args plus lines from --batch-file (or stdin via '-') are merged into all_urls; bare URLs are decoded with the preferred encoding before reaching the extractor loop.

Configuration input boundary: parseOpts merges /etc/youtube-dl.conf, user config (XDG_CONFIG_HOME/youtube-dl/config, ~/.config/youtube-dl.conf, %APPDATA% variants, ~/youtube-dl.conf), --config-location file, then argv — later entries override earlier ones; --ignore-config skips them.

The info dict is the canonical intermediate representation: extractor/common.py's class docstring specifies mandatory fields (id, title, and url-or-formats) plus ~50 optional fields and the _type discriminator values (video, playlist, multi_video, url, url_transparent, compat_list).

extract_info iterates self._ies calling ie.suitable(url) (compiled _VALID_URL regexes); the first match's extract() runs initialize() (geo-bypass, login) then _real_extract(url); results are stamped with extractor/webpage_url/extractor_key by add_default_extra_info.

process_ie_result recursively resolves indirection: 'url'/'url_transparent' results re-enter extract_info (possibly pinned to an ie_key); 'playlist'/'multi_video'/'compat_list' results go to __process_playlist which slices entries, injects playlist_* extra_info, and reprocesses each entry via __process_iterable_entry.

process_video_result normalizes a video info dict: forces string/numeric field types, sorts thumbnails, fills common fields, computes requested_subtitles, filters malformed formats, sorts formats with _sort_formats, and runs the parsed format selector (from build_format_selector) to produce formats_to_download or requested_formats for A+V merge.

process_info is the output boundary: it computes the filename via prepare_filename, writes .description/.annotations.xml/subtitle/.info.json/thumbnail files first, then calls dl() which instantiates the downloader chosen by get_suitable_downloader and copies http_headers via _calc_headers.

HttpFD.real_download streams to `filename + '.part'` opened just-in-time via sanitize_open, honoring resume (Range header + Content-Range validation), retry on 5xx/ECONNRESET/timeout, min/max filesize aborts, then try_rename to the final name and try_utime from Last-Modified.

Fragmented downloads (HlsFD, DashSegmentsFD, F4mFD, IsmFD) share FragmentFD, which keeps a `.ytdl` JSON bookkeeping file per incomplete download (extractor/downloader state, current_fragment, fragment_count) enabling resume and consistency checks.

Postprocessing output boundary: post_process chains info_dict['__postprocessors'] (e.g. FFmpegMergerPP for A+V merge, fixup PPs) before self._pps; each pp.run returns (files_to_delete, info); originals are deleted unless keepvideo.

State owners: the cookie jar (YoutubeDLCookieJar, Netscape format, optionally file-backed via --cookies) is owned by YoutubeDL._setup_opener; extractor/player caches (e.g. YouTube 'sigfuncs') live under the Cache section/key namespace; the download archive is a plain text append log.

Header/cookie hygiene is enforced at boundaries: FileDownloader.download documents stripping Cookie headers; _remove_cookie_header filters them from http_headers; header-supplied cookies are rescoped per-URL domain by _apply_header_cookies to prevent cross-domain leaks.

behavior_traces.summary: Three core flows were traced end-to-end: (1) CLI startup from argv to download; (2) a single-video download from URL through extraction, format selection, HTTP download, fixup and postprocessing to the archive write; (3) the YouTube signature-deciphering path that downloads player JS and interprets it with the built-in JSInterpreter. A fourth trace covers self-update.

claims.claim: Startup trace: `main()` -> `_real_main()` -> compat_register_utf8 + setproctitle -> parseOpts (reads /etc/youtube-dl.conf, user config, argv) -> header/batch-file handling -> option validation (netrc/password conflicts, numeric parsing of --limit-rate/--min-filesize, playlist bounds) -> postprocessor list assembly -> ydl_opts dict -> `with YoutubeDL(ydl_opts) as ydl` -> optional update_self / cache.remove -> ydl.download(all_urls) -> sys.exit(retcode).

YoutubeDL init trace: __init__ stores params, creates Cache, loads header cookies, warns on deprecated params, optionally spawns bidiv/fribidi for --bidi-workaround, then _setup_opener builds cookie jar (loading --cookies file), proxy handler, HTTPS/HTTP handlers, redirect handler and disables file://; auto_init then prints debug header and registers all extractor classes plus configured postprocessors and progress hooks, finishing with register_socks_protocols.

Download dispatch trace: download(url_list) -> extract_info -> ie.suitable(url) scan -> __extract_info (wrapped by __handle_extraction_exceptions) -> ie.extract(url) -> _real_extract -> process_ie_result -> dispatch on _type; for 'video' -> process_video_result -> format selection -> process_info -> dl() -> get_suitable_downloader(info) -> fd.download(name, info) -> real_download.

Playlist trace: process_ie_result sees _type playlist -> __process_playlist computes entries (list slice, PagedList.getslice, or islice over iterables, honoring --playlist-items) -> optional reverse/shuffle -> per entry: _match_entry(incomplete) filter -> __process_iterable_entry -> process_ie_result (recursion back into the same dispatch).

HTTP file download trace: FileDownloader.download checks overwrite/resume preconditions and applies randomized sleep_interval -> HttpFD.real_download -> establish_connection() (sanitized_Request with Range header, Content-Range validation, 416 fallback) -> download() loop: read block -> sanitize_open just-in-time -> stream.write -> slow_down rate limit -> _hook_progress -> loop until data_len -> try_rename .part -> try_utime -> 'finished' hook; errors route through RetryDownload/NextFragment/SucceedDownload control-flow exceptions.

YouTube signature trace: _decrypt_signature -> _cached(_extract_signature_function) -> filesystem cache 'sigfuncs' (keyed by player_url + signature-shape id) -> on miss _load_player downloads player JS -> _parse_sig_js regex-locates the sig function -> JSInterpreter.extract_function_from_code produces a Python callable -> the result is reduced to a char-permutation cache_spec and cached; _decrypt_nsig does the analogous flow for the throttling 'n' parameter.

Post-download trace: on dl() success, process_info applies fixup policy (FFmpegFixupStretchedPP for stretched_ratio, FFmpegFixupM4aPP for m4a_dash, FFmpegFixupM3u8PP for native HLS AAC) -> post_process runs __postprocessors then self._pps -> each pp.run returns files_to_delete which are removed unless keepvideo -> record_download_archive appends `extractor id` -> MaxDownloadsReached checked.

Self-update trace: update_self refuses non-zip/non-frozen installs -> GET https://yt-dl.org/update/LATEST_VERSION -> GET versions.json -> rsa_verify(json, signature, pinned UPDATES_RSA_KEY) -> sha256 the downloaded exe/bin blob -> write alongside the running binary (Windows: write .new + a youtube-dl-updater.bat that moves it after exit).

Error/abort trace: extraction errors funnel through __handle_extraction_exceptions (GeoRestrictedError gets a VPN hint, ExtractorError is reported, unexpected exceptions re-raise unless --ignore-errors); DownloadError propagates to main() -> sys.exit(1); MaxDownloadsReached exits 101; KeyboardInterrupt exits with an interrupted message.

testing_signals.summary: Testing is unittest-based, executed by nosetests (pynose on Python >=3.9). Coverage splits into offline unit tests (utils, aes, jsinterp, swfinterp, compat, options, YoutubeDL internals, URL matching) and a large live-download suite generated dynamically from each extractor's embedded _TEST/_TESTS dictionaries. Network-dependent suites are explicitly excluded from 'offlinetest'/'core' runs. CI on GitHub Actions spans CPython 2.6-3.12, PyPy and Jython on Ubuntu and Windows, plus a flake8 lint job; the download test-set is continue-on-error.

claims.claim: Test runner is nosetests: Makefile `test` runs `nosetests --verbose test` then flake8; devscripts/run_tests.sh selects core vs download sets via -I regex on test module names; tox.ini also drives nosetests with the same exclusion list.

Extractor test cases are embedded in extractor classes as _TEST/_TESTS dicts; InfoExtractor.get_testcases yields them, test/helper.py's gettestcases aggregates across gen_extractors(), and test_download.py dynamically synthesizes one TestDownload.test_<Name> method per case.

Download tests hit the real sites: they call ydl.extract_info on the case URL, retry up to 3 times on network-flavored errors (URLError, socket.timeout, HTTP 503), assert expected info_dict fields via expect_info_dict, verify the downloaded file exists and meets file_minsize, and optionally check an md5.

test/parameters.json supplies base params for tests (test=true limiting downloads to _TEST_FILE_SIZE, writeinfojson=true, socket_timeout=20, fixup=never); test/helper.py merges an optional untracked local_parameters.json for credentials.

Offline-only coverage is defined by exclusion: Makefile offlinetest and tox defaults exclude test_age_restriction, test_download, test_iqiyi_sdk_interpreter, test_socks, test_subtitles, test_write_annotations, test_youtube_lists and test_youtube_signature — i.e. anything needing network or live sites.

Unit-level suites cover utils (test_utils.py), JS interpreter (test_jsinterp.py), AES (test_aes.py against testdata/), SWF interpreter (test_swfinterp.py against test/swftests/), URL matching across extractors (test_all_urls.py), YoutubeDL internals (test_YoutubeDL.py), options parsing (test_options.py), netrc, cache, traversal and compat.

Test doubles exist in helper.py: FakeYDL (a YoutubeDL with auto_init=False that records download() calls and raises on trouble), FakeLogger, and expect_warnings/expect_info_dict assertion helpers that also fail when the extractor produces checkable fields missing from the test definition.

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) builds a matrix over CPython 2.6 through 3.12 plus pypy and jython, ubuntu-22.04 primary with windows-2022 and jython extras; it includes custom steps to build Python 2.6/2.7/3.next and install nose/pynose per version; download and jython legs are continue-on-error.
Lint is flake8 with repo-tuned ignores (E402,E501,E731,E741,W503) and excludes generated/excluded files; it runs as a separate CI job on Python 3.9 and as `make codetest`.

Notable gaps: there is no coverage tooling enabled by default (commented-out --with-coverage), most of the ~800 extractors rely solely on their embedded live tests (marked skip/_WORKING when broken), and legacy interpreters (Python 2.6, Jython) mean modern test runners can't even execute parts of the matrix.

risk_map.summary: The highest-risk areas are shell-outs (postprocessor --exec with shell=True, external downloader and ffmpeg command construction), credential handling (cookies, netrc, passwords), the self-update path that replaces the running binary, and the eval-adjacent JS/SWF interpreters. The codebase also carries heavy legacy weight: Python 2.6 compat shims, dead modules (swfinterp is only referenced by tests), and fragile regex-based scraping across ~800 site extractors that break silently when sites change.

claims.claim: ExecAfterDownloadPP.run executes the user's --exec command with subprocess.call(shell=True); the {} placeholder is shlex-quoted, but the rest of the command string is raw shell — a deliberate but real command-execution surface.

External downloaders and ffmpeg are spawned via subprocess.Popen with argv built from info_dict fields (url, http_headers, cookies); cookies are serialized into temp files or -cookies/-headers args, so a malicious extractor result could influence command lines, though lists (not shell strings) are used.

Self-update replaces the running executable with a network download; it is gated by an RSA signature over versions.json plus a per-file sha256 check, but trusts a hard-coded RSA key and yt-dl.org availability; the Windows path writes and spawns a .bat file that swaps the exe.

Cookie leak mitigations indicate a history of security issues: _remove_cookie_header strips Cookie from http_headers, _load_cookies scopes header-supplied cookies to the target domain (referencing yt-dlp advisory GHSA-v8mc-9377-rwjj), and YoutubeDLRedirectHandler drops Cookie on redirect; the file:// scheme is explicitly disabled citing issue #8227.

_UnsafeExtensionError enforces an extension whitelist on output files to prevent path traversal/arbitrary file overwrite (referencing yt-dlp advisory GHSA-79w7-vh3h-8g4j); --no-check-extensions sets the lenient flag to bypass it.
Aria2pFD connects to an aria2 daemon at http://localhost:6800 with an empty RPC secret and trusts the aria2p library being importable — local RPC without authentication.

JSInterpreter is a partial JS engine that executes extracted player code semantics; _extract_sig_fn even splices a regex-extracted 'useful values' snippet into the interpreted function — a YouTube player change silently breaks decryption, and malformed code raises JSInterpreter.Exception.

swfinterp.py (834 lines, SWFInterpreter) is effectively dead production code — the only importer in the tree is test/test_swfinterp.py; PhantomJSwrapper in extractor/openload.py survives only as a dependency of pornhub.py and a debug-header version probe.

Extractors are regex-fragile by design: _search_regex raises RegexNotFoundError on missing patterns and CONTRIBUTING.md explicitly warns that extractor breakage on site changes is expected; broken extractors are flagged via the _WORKING class attribute rather than removed.
--call-home/--verbose debug path sends requests to https://yt-dl.org/ip and /latest/version, disclosing the user's public IP to the project's own server.

Python 2.6 support is still load-bearing: compat.py shims, _workaround_optparse_bug9161, py2exe paths, and CI builds Python 2.6/2.7 from source — code paths that cannot be exercised on modern interpreters and constrain idioms (no f-strings, unicode_literals everywhere).

Passwords entered interactively (compat_getpass) or passed via -p/--password appear in argv and config files; _hide_login_info only scrubs them from verbose debug echoes, not from process listings or config storage.

extension_points.summary: The codebase is explicitly designed around plugin points. Primary: site extractors subclass InfoExtractor, define _VALID_URL + _real_extract, embed _TEST dicts, and register via an import line in extractor/extractors.py (plus optional lazy_extractors generation). Secondary: downloaders plug into PROTOCOL_MAP or the external-downloader _BY_NAME registry, postprocessors resolve by the '<key>PP' naming convention, and embedders hook progress_hooks, match_filter, custom logger, and the postprocessors param list.

claims.claim: New site support follows a documented recipe: create youtube_dl/extractor/<name>.py with an InfoExtractor subclass (class name ending in IE), define _VALID_URL regex and _real_extract, add a _TEST dict, and add one import line to extractor/extractors.py.

Extractor ordering is semantic: gen_extractor_classes returns _ALL_CLASSES in import order and the first suitable() match wins; GenericIE is appended last as the catch-all, so new extractors must be added before it implicitly by import placement.

Lazy loading is a compile-time extension artifact: devscripts/make_lazy_extractors.py generates youtube_dl/extractor/lazy_extractors.py from _ALL_CLASSES; this constrains extractor authors — overridden suitable() must import its own dependencies and avoid _VALID_URL references (documented in InfoExtractor's docstring).
SearchInfoExtractor is the extension base for 'keyword' providers (e.g. ytsearch): subclasses set _SEARCH_KEY and implement _real_extract over a query string, producing a playlist of url_results.

url_result()/playlist_result() are the delegation mechanism: an extractor can emit _type 'url' entries with an ie_key to hand a URL off to another extractor, enabling composite extractors without subclassing.

New downloaders subclass FileDownloader and implement real_download(filename, info_dict); protocol-based selection goes through PROTOCOL_MAP in downloader/__init__.py, while external-executable downloaders subclass ExternalFD (_make_cmd) and self-register in _BY_NAME keyed by executable basename.

New postprocessors subclass PostProcessor with a run(info)->(files_to_delete, info) contract; registration is by naming convention — a param dict {'key': 'X'} resolves to class XPP via get_postprocessor, and the CLI assembles the list in __init__.

Library/embedding hooks: YoutubeDL accepts progress_hooks (status dicts with downloading/error/finished and byte/eta/speed fields), a logger object, match_filter callable, extract_flat mode, and a postprocessors list — the documented embedding API.

Per-request behaviors can be injected through info_dict fields read downstream: http_headers, downloader_options (http_chunk_size), fragments, protocol, stretched_ratio, __postprocessors and __files_to_merge — extractors/downstream code cooperate through these keys.

Geo-bypass is itself an extension surface: extractors declare _GEO_COUNTRIES/_GEO_IP_BLOCKS/_GEO_BYPASS and _initialize_geo_bypass can be invoked mid-extraction with a context dict when restriction info is only known after the first response.

agent_handoff.summary: For an agent working in this repo: read CONTRIBUTING.md's developer instructions and extractor/common.py's giant docstring first; the info-dict contract and the 'first suitable() wins' ordering are the two invariants that matter most. Python 2.6-compatible style (unicode_literals, compat_* aliases, no f-strings, %-formatting) is mandatory and enforced by CI. Tests are nosetests; extractor changes get a live _TEST; run flake8 with the repo's setup.cfg ignores. Generated files (lazy_extractors.py, README.md, completions, man page) are produced by Makefile/devscripts — edit sources, not artifacts.

claims.claim: Read first: youtube_dl/extractor/common.py's InfoExtractor docstring (the entire info-dict schema), CONTRIBUTING.md 'DEVELOPER INSTRUCTIONS' + 'youtube-dl coding conventions', youtube_dl/YoutubeDL.py's options docstring, and youtube_dl/__init__.py _real_main for how params map to CLI flags.

Adding an extractor: new file in youtube_dl/extractor/, class name must end in 'IE', _VALID_URL with a named (?P<id>...) group is conventional, import the class in extractors.py (order = precedence), include a _TEST dict with a real URL; commit style is '[name] Add new extractor'.

Mandatory info-dict fields are id and title plus either url or formats; everything else must be extracted defensively (helpers: _search_regex with default=, try_get, traverse_obj, int_or_none/float_or_none) because extractors must tolerate missing optional data.

Run tests with `python test/test_download.py TestDownload.test_<Name>` for a single extractor; `make offlinetest` (or nosetests with the exclusion list) for network-free checks; full `make test` requires live network access and will fail on sites that changed since the pinned commit.

Lint with `flake8 .` honoring setup.cfg (ignores E402/E501/E731/E741/W503, excludes generated files); style is %-formatting, `from __future__ import unicode_literals` at top of every file, compat_* imports from youtube_dl/compat.py instead of py3-only stdlib paths.

Lazy-extractor constraint is a known trap: if you override suitable() or reference _VALID_URL oddly, devscripts/make_lazy_extractors.py output can break — keep suitable() self-importing and prefer plain _VALID_URL regexes; regenerate via `make lazy-extractors` or `python setup.py build_lazy_extractors`.

GenericIE must remain the last resort: _ALL_CLASSES appends it explicitly and many extractors emit url_result(ie=GenericIE.ie_key()) delegates; do not reorder extractors casually — the first regex match wins.

Generated artifacts to not hand-edit: youtube_dl/extractor/lazy_extractors.py (devscripts/make_lazy_extractors.py), README.md/CONTRIBUTING.md (devscripts/make_readme.py/make_contributing.py), docs/supportedsites.md (make_supportedsites.py), completions and man page (Makefile targets).

Safe edit boundaries: adding a new extractor file + extractors.py import is low-blast-radius; editing extractor/common.py, utils.py, YoutubeDL.py or downloader/common.py affects every site — keep changes additive, preserve py2.6 compatibility, and remember `_real_main` mutates the global std_headers dict and params dicts are shared references.

Debugging support built in: --verbose prints the debug header (version, git HEAD, Python, exe versions, proxy map), --write-pages/--dump-pages dump raw server responses, --print-traffic logs HTTP, and --youtube-print-sig-code prints the extracted signature function — use these before touching extractor code.

report.agent_prompt:
You are working in the youtube-dl repository (github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl), a dependency-free Python CLI that downloads video/audio from YouTube and ~1200 sites. It is also embeddable as a library (`import youtube_dl; YoutubeDL(params).download([url])`).

ARCHITECTURE: The pipeline is CLI args -> options.py parseOpts (merges /etc/youtube-dl.conf, user config, argv) -> youtube_dl/__init__.py:_real_main builds a ~120-key ydl_opts dict -> YoutubeDL (youtube_dl/YoutubeDL.py) orchestrates: it scans registered InfoExtractors (extractor/*, ~810 modules) calling ie.suitable(url) — first _VALID_URL regex match wins, GenericIE is last — then ie.extract() produces an 'info dict'. process_ie_result resolves _type discriminators (video/playlist/url/url_transparent) recursively; process_video_result normalizes fields and runs the format-selector DSL; process_info writes sidecars (.info.json, .description, subtitles, thumbnails) and invokes a FileDownloader chosen by PROTOCOL_MAP on info_dict['protocol'] (http->HttpFD, m3u8_native->HlsFD, m3u8->FFmpegFD, etc.) or an external downloader (aria2c/curl/wget/ffmpeg/httpie) spawned via subprocess. Downloads stream to file.part then rename; fragment downloads keep a .ytdl JSON state file. After success, post_process runs fixup + user postprocessors (ffmpeg extract-audio, embed-subs, metadata, --exec), then record_download_archive appends 'extractor id' to --download-archive.

KEY FILES: youtube_dl/extractor/common.py (InfoExtractor base — its docstring IS the info-dict spec; helpers like _download_webpage/_download_json/_search_regex), extractor/extractors.py (registry imports), extractor/__init__.py (gen_extractors, lazy loader), YoutubeDL.py (orchestrator + options docstring), downloader/{__init__,common,http,fragment,hls,external}.py, postprocessor/{__init__,ffmpeg,execafterdownload}.py, utils.py (6863-line toolbox incl. sanitized_Request, YoutubeDLCookieJar, _UnsafeExtensionError whitelist), compat.py (py2.6-3.x shims), jsinterp.py (JS interpreter used for YouTube signature deciphering in extractor/youtube.py), update.py (RSA-verified self-update), options.py, cache.py.

CONVENTIONS: Python 2.6-compatible code is REQUIRED — `from __future__ import unicode_literals` on every file, %-formatting not f-strings, compat_* imports for stdlib differences. To add a site: new extractor/<site>.py with class <Site>IE(InfoExtractor), _VALID_URL regex with (?P<id>...), _real_extract returning a dict with at least id+title+url-or-formats, a _TEST dict, and an import in extractors.py. Don't edit generated files (lazy_extractors.py, README.md, supportedsites.md, completions). Keep extractor suitable() methods self-contained for lazy_extractors generation.

TESTING: nosetests. `python test/test_download.py TestDownload.test_<Name>` runs an extractor's embedded live test (needs network); `make offlinetest` runs the network-free subset; `flake8 .` lints per setup.cfg. CI matrix spans Python 2.6-3.12 + PyPy/Jython. Live-site tests are inherently flaky at this pinned commit.

CAUTIONS: first-match-wins extractor ordering; --exec uses shell=True; params dicts and std_headers are shared mutable state; cookie/file:// mitigations in _setup_opener and _load_cookies are security-sensitive — preserve them.
